slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Now we can prove the Unit 2 constructions.

Perpendicular bisector: the arcs from A and B have equal radius, so the crossing points P and Q have PA = PB and QA = QB. Let N be the midpoint of AB and let m be the perpendicular line to AB through N, whose existence follows from the ruler/protractor assumptions, not from the compass construction being proved. Reflection in AB fixes each center and circle and exchanges their two intersection points P and Q. Reflection in m exchanges centers A and B and their equal-radius circles. It preserves each side of AB, so it fixes P and Q individually. Consequently P and Q lie on m. Thus PQ meets AB at M=N, between A and B and also between P and Q. Triangles APQ and BPQ are congruent by SSS, so angle APQ = angle BPQ. Ray PM is ray PQ, hence angle APM = angle BPM. With AP = BP and PM common, triangles APM and BPM are congruent by SAS. Therefore AM = BM, and the equal angles AMP and BMP form a linear pair, so each is 90 degrees. The reflection lemma establishes the result independently; the SSS/SAS calculation is an alternative verification.

Angle bisector and angle copy: the equal arcs make two triangles congruent by SSS, and CPCTC gives the equal angles.
